messages:
IncidentBot: Pager: routing.fallback.policy breach in us-west-2 · error-rate 4.7% · spillover observed to eu-west-1 · impacted hosted inference (text-gen) · paging oncall @Oncall SRE Maya :rotating_light:
Oncall SRE Maya: oncall here, ack. joining call in 2mins. cx impact? any major customers? :phone:
Customer Ops: seeing a jump in 5xxs for 2 customers (acme and climbly). ACME reports tokenization timeouts, climbly sees truncation. We have their request IDs.
Marco: logs: https://logs.redwood.example/stream/2315012345 (filtered) - looks like routing decisions changed at 23:02:10 UTC, requests intended for us-west-2 tierA started being routed to eu-west-1-tierB.
Sara: I see a config push at 23:01:58 from deploy-bot that updated routing policy weights (partial rollout). Could be correlated.
Jin: was there an autopilot/autoscaler event? autoscaler shows node flapping in us-west-2 from 23:01:30 -> 23:02:05.
Oncall SRE Maya: timeline so far: 23:01:30 autoscaler flapping; 23:01:58 routing-config rollout; 23:02:10 requests spilled to eu-west-1; 23:02:40 error rate spike.
Taylor: immediate mitigation: roll back routing-config rollout to previous stable at 23:03:05? Can someone trigger rollback?
Marco: rollback initiated by @Marco at 23:03:12 (deploy-bot ack). Rolling config -> previous.
IncidentBot: Deploy-bot: rollback job 98765 started.
Sara: while rollback runs, we should throttle spillover to eu-west-1 to avoid saturating eu infra. Suggest a temporary rate cap: set routing.max_spillover_qps=200.
Eng Runtime: can apply rate cap via rctl: `rctl set routing.max_spillover_qps 200 --scope=global` ; recommend 30s window.
Jin: applied rctl cap at 23:03:40, confirmed by mesh-proxy: "spillover_cap=200".
Oncall SRE Maya: current customer impact: ACME 12% error rate, Climbly 8% - trending down after rollback start but still elevated. Keep monitoring.
Marco: digging into decision logs: mismatch in model-compat table for tierB -> fallback model chosen was `redwood-2b-quant` but requests had prompt-length=12k tokens and that model rejects >8k, causing rejections -> 5xx from runtime. So misroute + incompatible fallback combo.
Sara: aha, so routing allowed fallback to model variant that doesn't support long context. Why was compatibility check skipped?
Eng Runtime: hypothesis: rolling routing weights changed target host set to include eu-west-1-tierB which was marked compatible at config-level but runtime capability metadata was stale. We had a recent metadata refresh bug (MR #1209) that didn't propagate kernel capability for quantized models.
Jin: corroborating logs: capability-refresh job failed at 22:59:12 with timeout to metadata service. However, deploy at 23:01:58 didn't revalidate.
Oncall SRE Maya: label hypotheses in-thread:
- Hypothesis A: Capability refresh failure + config rollout -> misroutes to incompatible fallback -> 5xxs.
- Hypothesis B: Autoscaler flapping reduced us-west-2 capacity causing routing to shift (expected) but routing policy didn't properly consult per-host capability -> misroutes.
- Hypothesis C: Rate cap absence allowed eu-west-1 to get saturated -> additional timeouts upstream.
Marco: quick check: list of affected route decisions (snip):
```
route_id=tx-9 host=eu-west-1-tierB fallback=redwood-2b-quant compatibility_check=SKIPPED
route_id=tx-13 host=eu-west-1-tierB fallback=redwood-2b-quant compatibility_check=SKIPPED
```
That SKIPPED flag is the smoking gun.
Taylor: mitigation summary (actions taken): rollback routing config (23:03:12), apply spillover cap (23:03:40), restart capability-refresh job (23:04:05), temporarily pin ACME/Climbly to us-west-2 until 23:15 UTC.
Customer Ops: pinned customers at 23:04:20, confirmed with customer relays. ACME reported partial recovery at 23:06.
Oncall SRE Maya: current ask list for RCA:
1) logs: full routing decision traces for 23:00-23:06 (Marco)
2) deploy diff + rollout window (Sara)
3) metadata refresh job logs + failure reason (Jin)
4) autoscaler evictions / node flapping details (Eng Runtime)
5) customer request IDs + sample traces (Customer Ops)
Please paste links in-thread.
Marco: uploaded routing traces: https://logs.redwood.example/trace/2315012345-routing-trace.gz
Sara: deploy diff: https://deploys.redwood.example/diffs/2315012345/ — rollout used new weight vector to prefer cheaper tierB under high load.
Jin: metadata job logs: https://ops.redwood.example/jobs/1209/logs - shows timeout to metadata-db endpoint due to ephemeral network blip to control-plane subnet.
Eng Runtime: autoscaler logs & node eviction events: https://metrics.redwood.example/autoscaler/us-west-2/2315012345.csv
Oncall SRE Maya: good. put hypothesis A as primary. Next immediate steps: 1) mark incident as "mitigated" when error-rate <1% for 10m. 2) prepare RCA skeleton.
Taylor: I'll start RCA skeleton now — will capture timeline, hypothesis, impact, root cause, fixes, and postmortem owners. Assigning owners: Marco (routing traces), Sara (deploy/process), Jin (metadata job + infra), Eng Runtime (compatibility-check tests + runtime guardrails), Customer Ops (customer impact collate).
IncidentBot: Incident state -> Mitigation in progress (error-rate 2.0% and decreasing).
Oncall SRE Maya: leaving a few follow-ups here. If error-rate goes up again, I'll resume pager. For now, escalate to P1 follow-up RCA.
Customer Ops: customers notified with status updates — ACME and Climbly asked for postmortem.
Marco: immediate followups in-thread:
- ActionItem: add pre-deploy compatibility verification that gates rollout if capability refresh job hasn't completed in last 5m. Owner: Sara.
- ActionItem: make routing decision logs include capability-check result (PASS/SKIPPED) in verbose mode. Owner: Marco.
- ActionItem: autoscaler backoff smoothing to avoid oscillation on short spikes. Owner: Eng Runtime.
Sara: I'll draft the pre-deploy gate change and propose it in RFC today.
Jin: will harden metadata job with retries and alert on control-plane connectivity errors.
Oncall SRE Maya: great. I'll convert this thread into the RCA doc template after we collect artifacts. Thanks everyone — leaving notes and handing to postmortem owners. :white_check_mark:
IncidentBot: Incident closed to active pager at 23:12:09 — monitoring until 23:32:09 for regression.
